findings.title: Deleting the cache does not refresh the connectedCalendars query, so the UI stays stale
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`. The disconnect mutation in the same file invalidates `connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, but the delete-cache mutation does not. It relies on the caller's `onChanged`. `CalendarListContainer` passes one that invalidates the query (`apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88`). The event-type Advanced tab renders `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` with no `onChanged` (`packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-378`). There the user sees 'Cache deleted successfully', but `cacheUpdatedAt` is unchanged. The dropdown still shows the old 'Last updated' time and the 'Delete cached data' item. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete-cache mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled`, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: Delete-cache action is now exposed where connection modification is disabled
findings.body: The old code hid the whole actions area when `disableConnectionModification` was true. The event-type Advanced tab passes `disableConnectionModification={true}` (`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375`). With the new `hasCache` path, the dropdown still renders there with 'Delete cached data'. That deletes the credential-wide cache from an event-type-scoped settings screen that was meant to be read-only for credentials. The wrapper also does not consider `isDisabled` (the disabled scope). If this is intended, say so. If not, gate `hasCache` on `!disableConnectionModification`, or add a separate prop for it.

findings.title: Timestamp hard-codes the en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale, even though the label goes through `t()`. Non-English users get US-formatted dates. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) or an existing date helper. The `interpolation: { escapeValue: false }` is needed here, but the timezone is the browser's and is not labelled.

findings.title: Plain Error becomes a 500; use TRPCError
findings.body: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` is mapped by tRPC to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. A missing or foreign credential is a client error. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `FORBIDDEN`. Otherwise it is logged and alerted as a server fault.

findings.title: Handler writes through prisma directly instead of the cache repository; input schema is inline
findings.body: The PR body says 'use repository pattern', but this handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly. `CalendarCacheRepository` (and its mock, which already has `deleteManyByCredential`) is the abstraction for this table. The input schema is also defined inline in `_router.tsx:29` as `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })`. The sibling procedures use separate `*.schema.ts` files (`connectedCalendars.schema.ts`, `setDestinationCalendar.schema.ts`). Ownership is checked correctly (`userId: user.id`) and only that credential's rows are deleted.

findings.title: updateMany on SelectedCalendar after every cache refresh has no visible consumer
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. Nothing reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, and the `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields added to `UserRepository` (`user.ts:899-900`) and to `UserWithCalendars` are not used in `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts`. So each webhook-driven refresh pays an extra write across all of the credential's selected calendars for nothing visible, and the added select fields are dead. It also relies on Prisma treating an empty `data` as an `@updatedAt` bump, which is non-obvious. Drop it, or explain what depends on it.

findings.title: Legacy rows all get the migration time as 'last updated'
findings.body: Existing CalendarCache rows are backfilled with `NOW()`. For up to a month of old entries, the dropdown will show 'Last updated: <migration time>' when the data may be much older. Backfilling from `expiresAt - interval '30 days'` (CACHING_TIME is 30 days, `calendar-cache.repository.ts:15`) would be more accurate. Also, the generated header comment ('required column ... without a default value') contradicts the statement below it, which does add a default.

findings.title: Script is macOS-only, fails with exit 0, and depends on cwd
findings.body: `sed -i ''` (line 68) is BSD syntax and breaks on GNU sed. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the cwd, not the script, so running it from the repo root edits or creates a `.env` outside the repo. `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so the 'Failed to extract URL' and rate-limit branches report success to callers. When reusing a running tmole, a missing `/tmp/tmole.log` gives an empty URL. Resolve paths from `$(dirname "$0")`, use a portable sed, and exit non-zero on the failure paths.

findings.title: Mock's disabled-cache path is bypassed by the handler
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly (`connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28`) rather than going through the factory that selects the mock when calendar-cache is disabled. The mock's `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is therefore never used, and the extra groupBy runs on every connectedCalendars call, whether or not the cache is enabled. Confirm this is intended, or use the same selection path as the other callers.

contracts.action: Delete cached data (new tRPC mutation viewer.calendars.deleteCache)
contracts.equivalent_path: credentials.delete via DisconnectIntegration, which invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations in onSettled (packages/features/apps/components/DisconnectIntegration.tsx:36-39)
contracts.before_after: The handler verifies in the same request that credential.userId equals the session user (lines 17-26), then runs deleteMany scoped to that credentialId (28-30). It does not delete other credentials' rows and does not run when the credential is missing. There is no re-check between findFirst and deleteMany, but ownership of a credential id does not change. The UI path does not invalidate the query itself.
contracts.visible_effect: The toast says 'Cache deleted successfully'. The 'Last updated' value only refreshes if the caller's onChanged invalidates connectedCalendars. CalendarListContainer does; EventAdvancedTab does not.
contracts.failure_mode: On rejection, onError shows 'Error deleting cache'; nothing is lost. After deletion, getFreeBusyResult falls back to a live fetch on a cache miss (CalendarService.ts:475-480), so availability keeps working but is slower until the next refresh.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars handler enriched with cacheUpdatedAt via groupBy on CalendarCache
contracts.equivalent_path: Other CalendarCacheRepository callers that go through CalendarCache.init, which can return the mock when the cache is disabled
contracts.before_after: It adds one groupBy query per connectedCalendars call using a directly constructed repository. The result is joined by credentialId and null when absent. The cache upserts set updatedAt through @updatedAt on update, and the column defaults on create.
contracts.visible_effect: The Google Calendar dropdown shows 'Last updated' only when a cache row exists.
contracts.failure_mode: If the groupBy throws, the whole connectedCalendars query fails and the settings page errors. Previously this handler had no such extra dependency.

contracts.action: Replace DisconnectIntegration with CredentialActionsDropdown in both the calendar card and the error Alert
contracts.equivalent_path: Old inline gating: `!delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification` for the card, and only `!delegationCredentialId` for the Alert
contracts.before_after: The disconnect logic moves into the dropdown, with the same gating via canDisconnect. The Alert path now also honours disableConnectionModification, which it did not before. The dropdown also shows the cache items when connection modification is disabled (event-type tab), which the old code never rendered.
contracts.visible_effect: The trash button becomes an ellipsis menu. In the event-type tab a menu appears for Google credentials with a cache.
contracts.failure_mode: The disconnect confirmation closes immediately on confirm, and errors surface only as a toast. The old code also closed on error, so this matches.

contracts.action: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) at the end of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache
contracts.equivalent_path: Other SelectedCalendarRepository writes by credential in the same service (upsertManyForEventTypeIds, updateById)
contracts.before_after: It writes to every SelectedCalendar of the credential, including delegation and event-type-scoped rows, after the cache loop. If the cache fetch throws, this is skipped.
contracts.visible_effect: None found: no reader of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt in the UI path.
contracts.failure_mode: If updateMany rejects, fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache rejects even though the cache was already written, so callers such as webhook handling and unwatch see a failure after the cache succeeded.

summary:
I read all 17 files and found one fix-level bug and several smaller issues. The calendar cache dropdown works on the main settings page. The delete-cache handler checks that the credential belongs to the session user and only deletes that credential's rows.

- **Stale UI after delete (fix):** `CredentialActionsDropdown` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` after deleting the cache. It relies on the caller's `onChanged`. The event-type Advanced tab passes none, so there the 'Last updated' time and the delete item stay on screen after a success toast.
- **Delete action in read-only view (consider):** The event-type tab passes `disableConnectionModification={true}`. The old code hid all actions there. The dropdown now still offers 'Delete cached data'.
- **Smaller points (consider):** These cover the hard-coded `en-US` date format, the plain `Error` that becomes a 500, the handler bypassing `CalendarCacheRepository`, and the migration backfilling old rows with `NOW()`.
- **Possibly dead write (consider):** The `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` update has no reader I could find, and the extra select fields in `user.ts` and `UserWithCalendars` are unused.
- **Script (consider):** `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` is macOS-only, depends on the working directory and exits 0 on failure.

The `dev:cron` switch to `npx tsx` and the locale strings looked fine.
